Name: Deepak Mehta
Question: How does shiridi Sai Baba answer our prayers? I have been begging him for a solution since 7 yrs of my marriage. I have got nothing but more and more trouble. I know this is my karma, but why doesn't Baba help me get through this
Answer: The root cause of a lot of our woes is that we seek the locus of control externally instead of looking inwards. No one is going to solve your problems for you. People will give you advice. Friends and family will comfort you. Faith in god or a higher power will provide you solace. But unless you resolve to take charge of your own destiny, nothing will move. Your demons won’t go away and you will be left blaming everything, apart from yourself, for your misery. You’ve had marital problems for 7 years now. That is almost 10% of your entire life. Have you sat back and wondered why is it so? Is it a core compatibility issue? Or is there a gaping hole in your communication and expectations? The wise Kabir Das said, “मोको कहाँ ढूंढें बन्दे, मैं तो तेरे पास में।” | “Why do you search for me elsewhere, I am but within you!” I am an atheist. But I still understand why people choose to believe in a higher power. There are times when the going goes so tough that you need someone to look up to. To have someone to complain to and seek help from and something to assure you that things will be alright. It is but a psychological trick to find that extra bit of assurance and the strength needed to tackle the demons plaguing you. God, whomever you pray to, is akin to a cheerleader. They provide you the morale boost to keep going when everything seems bleak. But they cannot play your game for you. God is like the ones standing on the sidelines and edging you on during the final leg of the marathon when your legs refuse to move an inch. Their voices and their cries of encouragement allow your body to extend beyond its limits and provide you with that last-minute adrenaline boost to cross the line. But they cannot run the race for you. God is like the wind in your sails that propels your boat. But you need to take charge and man the sails and steer yourself to reach your destination. They cannot take over the boat for you. In the end, you can only ask god for serenity, wisdom, and strength. But the onus of getting up and taking charge of your life is in your own hands.

Question: What do you think about the people who think that COVID-19 is a hoax?
Answer: There’s an old Bollywood song that goes, कुछ तो लोग कहेंगे, लोगों का काम है कहना छोड़ो बेकार की बातों में, कहीं बीत ना जाये रैना (People will always say something or the other, that is what they do. Set aside these idle talks, lest the night is wasted too.) Social media has given everyone a platform to voice their opinion. Even the shittiest of thoughts that a random earthling has can be put out for the rest of the world to see with just a few clicks. But there is only so much useful, informational content out there. Limited human intellectual capacity. And social media platforms benefit from higher engagement, so they incentivize even the mundane, the repetitive, and the downright stupid. “Some people” believe that the Earth is flat, despite the fact that we have photographs from outer space proving it isn’t. “Some people” still claim that the Earth is just a few thousand years old when there is conclusive scientific and archeological evidence that they are off by a million degrees. “Some people” still promulgate that the moon landing was a hoax and no amount of logical reasoning or proof will make them change their mind. “Some people” vocally oppose vaccines because they think it causes autism, ignoring the advice of thousands of scientists and researchers and medical professionals, people who know far more about what they are talking, and you can’t convince them otherwise. “Some people” are idiots. I ignore “some people”.

Question: What are some ways to cope with living by yourself?
Answer: The biggest mindshift you can start with is by redefining the question itself. If you think of living by yourself as undesirable, something you have to “cope with”, it’s already a tough road ahead for you. Further paraphrase “living by yourself” to “living with yourself”. You are not alone, you are in your own company. So we basically end up with a radically shifted viewpoint. “What are some ways to enjoy living with yourself?” This is one of the things everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime. Very rarely do you get the chance to be completely with yourself. As a kid, you stay with your parents. Then you’re off to college where you’d be sharing a room or dorm with other students. You start working and its economically the prudent choice to share an apartment with other working professional. Then you get married and share your space with your spouse. Then your kids. Where in all this is the time to truly figure out who you are? They say “you are the average of the 5 people you spend the most time with”. And if none of those 5 is your own self, you risk becoming an amalgamation of various personalities, a derivative being. Living with yourself gives you a chance to discover who you truly are. Pay attention to how you are when there is no one around and you don’t need any filters or masks. Get in touch with your deepest thoughts. Notice how you spend your time. I have been living on my own for 1.5 years now and it can be a really pleasurable and introspective experience. That said, it is not easy (nothing ever really is!) There are times when you feel lonely, when you desire the comfort of companionship, when you feel the urge to talk to someone. However, all of that can be remediated. Because we live in the era of instant connectivity, you can call up your family or friends and see them. You can get on a bunch of dating apps and find someone to have a conversation or a casual encounter with. Boredom, similarly, can be worked on. You need to figure out your hobbies. Create your own personal mini-verses in the house. A comfortable sofa and comfoter so that you can just snuggle up and watch the latest movie or re-runs of your favorite show. A cozy nook for reading. A quiet breezy corner where you can meditate. You can join interest groups and find interesting people to form new connections with. Go hiking. Volunteer at an animal shelter. Head out alone and explore the city on weekends. Plan a solo trip. Pick up the guitar and strum. Paint. Sculpt. Enroll for online classes. Have a teleparty. The avenues are endless, it is up to you to reach out and give them a try. Godspeed stranger!
